title: Git plugin
goal:
Spec §11.3 and §14 phase 4. Required outcomes:
- `crates/simplefile-core/src/git.rs` (and its status cache) becomes the plugin's Rust backend.
- The Git workbench view, view model, detachable window and the logic in `MainWindow.Git.cs` move into the plugin's C# assembly, rebuilt as code-built UI (or `XamlReader.Load` strings), because compiled XAML from plugin folders fails (spec §5.3).
- The host gains the side-panel slot (`IPanelProvider`, one visible panel, host-or-window toggle, resize grip, replacing the inline `GitPanel` in `MainWindow.xaml` and `GitWorkbenchWindow` with a generic `PluginPanelHost`/`PluginPanelWindow`) and the row-decoration slot (`IRowDecorationProvider`, `Row.DecorationText`/`DecorationBrushKey` replacing `Row.GitText`, batched per folder, 250 ms budget, populating `ContextMenuRequest.FolderFlags` and `SelectionDecorationPlugins` so `when` expressions like `folderFlag(inRepository)` and `hasDecoration` work).
- Contributions: ten commands, a context-menu group with `when` expressions, a toolbar toggle, the panel, and a startup-activated row decoration provider. Setting `enabled` replaces `EnableGitIntegration`, migrated on first run.
- Core loses the 11 Git IPC methods, `GitText`, the Git menu, commands, inline panel and toolbar button; schema counts, bindings, parity gate, docs and CI follow.
- Packaging stages and pre-approves `payload\plugins\com.sumafile.git`; tests and UI smoke assertions cover the plugin path end to end, plus a no-plugin smoke.

User rulings (2026-11-09, recorded in spec §5.1/§12 and the review notes): plugin UI hand-offs in the WinUI-free SDK stay `object`-typed at 1.0.0 with run-time WinUI type checks, so `IPanelProvider` and `IRowDecorationProvider` follow the same pattern; plugin C# projects reference Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK, Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools and CommunityToolkit.Mvvm compile-only (ExcludeAssets=runtime, PrivateAssets=all) and use the host's copies through PluginLoadContext's shared prefixes. Update the pinned SDK surface snapshot deliberately.

User requirement (2026-11-09), to be done in the FIRST task(s) of this phase, test-first, before any Git work: no plugin file is stored outside the program installation folder. SumaFile installs per user (NSIS InstallDir $LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\SumaFile-WinUI, WiX InstallScope perUser), so the install folder is writable. The user chose "all plugin files" and "uninstall removes everything":
- Plugin roots: drop the separate user root %LOCALAPPDATA%\SumaFile\plugins (PluginDiscovery.UserRoot/DefaultRoots). Bundled and user-installed plugins both live in <install>\plugins (PluginDiscovery.InstallRoot, AppContext.BaseDirectory). Installing a .sfplugin, Remove and "open plugins folder" (SettingsWindow.Plugins.cs UserPluginRoot, PluginPackageInstaller) target <install>\plugins. Trust must stay keyed on bundled.json, never on location: a plugin the user installs into <install>\plugins still needs consent; installing a package whose id is a bundled plugin's id, or that would overwrite a bundled folder, is refused; Remove refuses bundled plugins. If the install folder is not writable, installing fails with a clear message.
- Plugin data: PluginDiscovery.DataRoot defaults to <install>\plugins-data (each backend's data folder, e.g. the remote plugin's remote-profiles.db). The approvals file (PluginApprovalStore.DefaultPath) defaults to <install>\plugin-approvals.json. plugins.log moves under the install folder too (startup-timing.log is the app's own and may stay); update every script and check that reads plugins.log (startup smoke, check-winui-startup-budget and others). The SUMAFILE_PLUGIN_ROOTS, SUMAFILE_PLUGIN_DATA_ROOT and SUMAFILE_PLUGIN_APPROVALS_PATH overrides keep working for tests and smokes, and smokes must still never write into the real install folder or the developer's real data.
- No migration from the old %LOCALAPPDATA%\SumaFile\plugins, plugins-data or plugin-approvals.json: the plugin system never shipped in a release (only the unreleased branch commit 46860dc used them). The app never reads or writes those old locations again and does not delete them. Record this in the spec.
- Installers: NSIS reinstall/upgrade still replaces each bundled plugin folder whole and must keep user-installed plugins, plugins-data and plugin-approvals.json; NSIS uninstall already removes $INSTDIR whole (keep that, so uninstall leaves no plugin file). WiX: a major upgrade must keep those user files, and uninstall must remove them (for example util:RemoveFolderEx on the plugins, plugins-data folders and the approvals file and log, scoped to uninstall only, not upgrade). Update the installer comments that say the user root under %LOCALAPPDATA% is never touched, scripts/check-winui-packaging.mjs, and the MSI/NSIS smokes to prove: upgrade keeps a user plugin and its data; uninstall leaves nothing under the install folder. Credentials in Windows Credential Manager are not files and stay where they are.
- Update spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-plugin-system-design.md everywhere it names %LOCALAPPDATA%\SumaFile\plugins, plugins-data or plugin-approvals.json (roots list near line 71, the data directory, the approval store, installer section, the remote profiles decision), README and SECURITY docs if they mention them, and the tests (PluginEnvironmentTests, PluginPackageInstallerTests and others).

Carry-overs from the phase 3 whole-phase review. Fix them in the first tasks, test-first, and the phase review must confirm them:
(a) Parked for phase 4: #82 plugin code runs inline inside host layout passes; #78/#84 CollapsedPluginSidebarSections mutated on the UI thread during a background settings save; #65/#69 Changed raised up to ~10 s after LoadFailed; #63 load-failure teardown runs outside _ops; and EnsurePrimaryItem re-adding a toolbar button the user removed (phase 4 adds a toolbar toggle). Details in .superpowers/phase-3-remote/prior-minors.md and the phase 1 review notes.
(b) Remote Manager close during a transfer leaks the server session (plugins/remote/ui/SumaFile.Remote/Views/RemoteManagerWindow.cs:355-378, plugins/remote/backend/src/session.rs:171-210): disconnect fails with "Remote session is busy" because the cancelling transfer still holds the provider lock. Make close wait (bounded) for the cancelled transfer to release and then disconnect, as spec §11.2 promises.
(c) Pin the 1.0.4 Credential Manager blob format with a golden test using fixed bytes (plugins/remote/backend/src/secrets.rs), not write_secret round trips.
(d) Verify, and fix if needed, that a plugin dialog shown through DialogHost (src-winui/SimpleFile.App/DialogHost.cs, PluginWindowHost.cs) releases the app-wide dialog gate when its window is closed by the host (Disable, rescan, load failure, main-window close) with the dialog open; guard the dialog.Hide() dispatcher callback in RunWithProgressAsync. Phase 4 adds detachable plugin panel windows, so this matters more.
(e) Harden the remote UI smoke (src-winui/SimpleFile.App/MainWindow.UiSmoke.Remote.cs, scripts/smoke-winui-ui.ps1): step 11 must assert every baseline SumaFile.Remote.* credential target still exists; the script removes the Smoke SFTP credential in its own finally even if the App is killed or crashes; a cleanup exception is reported even when a step already failed; every cross-process await is bounded.
(f) Small leftovers: CommandSurfaceLayout.cs:178 previousDefault literal can no longer match; simplefile-service declares the unused sha2 dependency; RemoteManagerViewModel.cs:900 ReplaceLocalEntries comment is wrong; Get-BundledPluginFreshnessFiles skips SumaFile.Remote.deps.json; CopyRemotePluginFixture and CopyBundledPlugins never prune stale copies; parity-gate.md header vs inventory.md command counts.
(g) Flaky test PluginManagerTests.ArchivePlugin_SuccessfulRegistration_LogsTheRegisteredFormats: wait for the log line instead of BackendRunning.
(h) Startup budget: the plugins-discovered span is 15 ms locally but measured 74.2 ms on the hosted windows-2025 runner at 46860dc (before the phase 3 fix wave; no hosted run since). Phase 4 adds a third bundled plugin with a startup-activated row decoration provider. Keep that provider's activation and first decoration batch off the critical path before the plugins-discovered mark, keep check:winui-startup-budget passing locally, and apply spec §5.2's lever (warm first-use render costs while the file service starts) if it fits naturally. Do not raise the budget.

Context: phases 2 (7-Zip) and 3 (FTP/SFTP) are complete; phase 3 Tasks 1-12 are committed in 46860dc, Tasks 13-15 and the phase 3 fix wave are uncommitted in the working tree (never commit). Plans: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-08-plugin-system-phase-2-sevenzip.md and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-09-plugin-system-phase-3-remote.md; reports in .superpowers/phase-2-sevenzip/ and .superpowers/phase-3-remote/. Reuse what they built: plugin staging (scripts/lib/plugin-staging.ps1, scripts/build-plugins.ps1), bundled.json trust, the sumafile-plugin and sumafile-transfer crates, the code-built plugin UI pattern of plugins/remote/ui (SumaFile.Remote and SumaFile.Remote.Model), plugin-owned secondary windows (IPluginWindows), the sidebar and settings-page slots, and the remote smoke structure. Use plugins/remote as the layout model (backend, ui, test fixtures). Migrate the existing EnableGitIntegration setting on first run. Update the spec where decisions refine it.

areas.prompt: crates/simplefile-core/src/git.rs and its status cache, every caller in crates/simplefile-core and crates/simplefile-service (dispatch handlers, params, session hooks, the 11 Git IPC methods), and their tests. Map what moves into a Rust plugin backend built on crates/sumafile-plugin (use plugins/remote/backend as the layout model), how status is batched per folder for row decorations, which git executable discovery and process rules apply, and what core keeps.

Everything Git in src-winui: MainWindow.Git.cs, the Git workbench view and view model, GitWorkbenchWindow, the inline GitPanel in MainWindow.xaml, Row.GitText and how it renders, the Git menu, commands, context-menu entries, the toolbar button, EnableGitIntegration settings, BackendSession/IPC Git calls and generated bindings, and the tests. Map which XAML must become code-built UI (compiled XAML cannot load from plugin folders, spec section 5.3) following plugins/remote/ui, and which host services the Git plugin assembly needs.

src-winui/SimpleFile.PluginSdk (contracts, pinned surface snapshot) and src-winui/SimpleFile.PluginHost plus how SimpleFile.App renders plugin contributions (MainWindow.Plugins*.cs, PluginWindowHost, DialogHost, sidebar and settings slots, CommandSurfaceLayout, EnsurePrimaryItem, ContextMenuRequest, when-expression evaluation with folderFlag/hasDecoration, SelectionDecorationPlugins). Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-plugin-system-design.md sections 4, 7, 8 and 11.3. Map what IPanelProvider (one visible panel, host-or-window toggle, resize grip, PluginPanelHost/PluginPanelWindow) and IRowDecorationProvider (Row.DecorationText/DecorationBrushKey, batched per folder, 250 ms budget, FolderFlags) need, plus the phase 3 carry-overs (a) and (d) and the startup path for a startup-activated provider. Also map every place that resolves plugin locations (PluginDiscovery.DefaultRoots/UserRoot/InstallRoot/DataRoot, PluginApprovalStore.DefaultPath, plugins.log, PluginPackageInstaller install/Remove, Settings > Plugins folder links, bundled.json trust) for moving all plugin files into the install folder.

The 11 Git IPC methods across ipc/schema/v1, scripts/check-ipc-schema.mjs, scripts/generate-ipc-bindings.mjs and generated bindings, docs/winui-migration (parity-gate.md, inventory.md), README, scripts/lib/plugin-staging.ps1, scripts/build-plugins.ps1 and callers, scripts/check-winui-packaging.mjs, packaging/winui (NSIS, WiX), .github/workflows, scripts/smoke-winui-ui.ps1 and MainWindow.UiSmoke*.cs, scripts/check-winui-startup-budget.mjs. Map what removing the Git methods and staging a third bundled plugin (com.sumafile.git) changes, how a smoke drives Git end to end (a temporary repository created with the git CLI), plus a no-git-plugin smoke and the phase 3 smoke carry-over (e). Also map how the NSIS and WiX installers and their smokes treat files under the install folder on upgrade and uninstall, and every script that reads plugins.log or a %LOCALAPPDATA%\SumaFile plugin path.

extraVerify: 7. Also run every additional staging script, crate test and smoke variant that the phase plan adds (for example scripts/build-plugins.ps1, scripts/test-plugin-staging.ps1, the git backend tests, the end-to-end Git smoke and the no-git-plugin smoke, the remote and 7-Zip smokes), plus npm run check:winui-startup-budget, npm run smoke:winui-file-ops and npm run release:build, and report each. Also run the NSIS and MSI smokes that prove upgrade keeps a user plugin and its data and uninstall leaves nothing, and report each.
